html:
SMTO-SKL-0171 — GitHub wouldn't merge this pull request

GUID: 6540d2e0-5b1f-5e98-8d15-8d8bde087fc1
Slug: github-pull-not-mergeable
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • GitHub didn't confirm the merge. The pull request may already be merged or closed, or something is blocking it, such as conflicts, failing checks, missing reviews or branch rules.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the pull request on github.com and check whether it's already merged or closed. If it's already merged, there's nothing more to do, and merging again isn't possible.
  2. Look at the merge area at the bottom of the pull request to see what blocks it: conflicts, failing checks, or reviews still needed. GitHub lists the exact reasons it won't merge.
  3. Fix what's blocking it, or ask the repository owner to, then ask SMTO to merge again once GitHub shows it can be merged. GitHub will only merge when the repository's rules are met.

What success looks like

  • The pull request shows as merged on github.com.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the repository owner. Don't try to get around the repository's branch rules or merge a different version instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The merge was refused: the pull request was already merged or not open at preflight, GitHub returned HTTP 405 for the merge, or the merge response did not report merged=true.

What this means

  • Merge returns HTTP 405 or a response whose merged field is not true. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Merge returns HTTP 405 or a response whose merged field is not true.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact head, merge response, conflicts, checks, reviews and branch rules.

How to fix it

  • GitHubService.dispatch raises pull_not_mergeable when the preflight read shows merged or state != open, when the PUT pull-request merge endpoint returns 405, or when its response lacks merged=true. Inspect PR state, mergeability, checks, required reviews and branch protection for the same head; do not bypass protection or substitute another head before a new deliberate merge.
  • Inspect PR state, conflicts, checks, required reviews and branch rules. Do not bypass branch protection or substitute another head.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Required conditions are met for the same intended head before another deliberate merge.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
